task.name: Applying an accepted decomposition proposal is a separate mutation from producing it
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2686
---

## What

An operator who accepts a decomposition proposal has forge apply it: create one issue per
proposed slice, write the dependency edges where the scheduler reads them, close the original
as decomposed, and record the disposition. Producing the proposal is separate work; this is
the mutation that acts on it.

## Why

Producing a proposal and applying one carry different risks. A proposal is an artifact the
operator reads and can ignore at no cost. Applying it mutates the issue tracker — new issues,
declared edges, the original closed — and a bad proposal that was applied costs more to undo
than one that was declined. Separating them lets the proposal ship first and be measured
against whether accepted splits actually land, before anything acts on it automatically.

The separation also keeps each piece within single-story scope. Carried together, the
deliberation, the proposal schema, dependency inference, issue creation, edge writing and
audit disposition are the shape the complexity pause exists to catch.

## Acceptance criteria

- Accepting a proposal creates one issue per proposed slice, each carrying that slice's title
  and scope boundary.
- Every dependency edge the proposal declares is written into the created issue bodies at
  creation time, in the form the sprint scheduler reads, rather than added afterwards.
- The original story is closed as decomposed, distinguishable from one closed as completed.
- Nothing is created without an explicit operator acceptance. A proposal that is declined, or
  left unanswered until the pause resolves by any other route, creates nothing and leaves the
  original story intact and runnable.
- A failure partway through leaves a state the operator can act on rather than a half-applied
  split: what was created is reported, and the original story is not closed unless every slice
  was created and every declared edge written.
- The audit records the proposal as applied and its disposition, so a later measurement can ask
  whether accepted splits landed.

## Example

```
PAUSE     → #2541 scored 10, scope exceeded. Proposal (4 slices) attached.
OPERATOR  → forge decide 7c1e04b9d3af accept

APPLIED   → created #2900  extract the portable diagnosis record
            created #2901  route diagnosis through the record      depends_on #2900
            created #2902  port the CLI surface                    depends_on #2900
            created #2903  cross-project acceptance                depends_on #2901, #2902
            closed  #2541  decomposed
            audit   proposal applied, disposition accepted
```

Declining instead creates nothing and leaves #2541 exactly as it was.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 does not define the terminal result of accept. In src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_complexity_gate.py, every decision other than approve currently falls through to _decompose_result(success=False). Because src/theforge/sprint/runner.py::_returned_for_decomposition recognizes only decompose, a successfully applied accept would be classified FAILED; returning None instead would incorrectly continue planning and implementing the now-closed original story.
  Suggestion: Specify and test an explicit terminal applied result for successful accept and an actionable terminal failure result for partial application. Account for direct-run and sprint classification in src/theforge/cli/run.py and src/theforge/sprint/runner.py if a distinct applied outcome is required.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The existing gate and decomposition assessment support file-backed TaskStory objects with github_issue=None, but Step 4 offers accept whenever an assessment exists. The proposed gh-only application cannot close such an original or satisfy the tracker mutation contract.
  Suggestion: Offer accept only when task.github_issue is present and the source supports GitHub mutation, or add a real story-source mutation abstraction. Add a seam test proving file-backed proposals never offer or execute accept.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 introduces a new raw gh issue-close path without accounting for the repository-wide check_spike_closure boundary. A high-complexity spike can reach this gate; bypassing the guard violates the enforced close invariant and can result in the issue being reopened, so the original is not durably closed as decomposed.
  Suggestion: Route the close through theforge.spike_guard.check_spike_closure and record a valid follow-up outcome referencing an eligible created slice before closing. Test both ordinary and spike originals.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The stated retry-duplication risk is only partially mitigated: markers and a persisted slice-to-issue map make prior creations identifiable, but the plan never says retries must reuse or skip those mapped slices, and no retry test enforces that behavior.
  Suggestion: Make application explicitly idempotent by restoring the persisted map, verifying marked issues, and creating only missing slices; add a retry-after-partial-failure test.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 vaguely copies tracker context 'where safe' but does not require each created issue to receive exactly one runnable type label. The shape gate rejects unlabeled issues, so valid-looking slices may be unusable immediately after creation.
  Suggestion: Define how labels and other required issue-shape metadata are derived, and test that each created slice passes the target issue-shape requirements.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The plan never says what CoordinatorResult the accept path returns. In preflight_complexity_gate.py:477-492 the branch is binary: approve returns None (run continues), anything else falls through to _decompose_result. Continuing the run after the original issue was closed would plan and implement a closed story; falling through unchanged returns success=False with decision='accept', which sprint/runner.py:3393 _returned_for_decomposition does not recognise (it compares only against PREFLIGHT_GATE_DECOMPOSE), so the sprint would report an applied split as an ordinary failed story rather than as decomposed.
  Suggestion: Decide the accept terminal result explicitly in Step 2 — return a terminal PREFLIGHT result analogous to _decompose_result — and extend _returned_for_decomposition (and the cli/run.py:318 gate-decision read) to treat an applied accept as a decomposed outcome, not a failure. Add a runner-level assertion to Step 6.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 describes slice-issue content as title, scope boundary, mapped criteria and 'runnable tracker context from the original issue where safe', but never names labels or milestone. Created issues without a recognized type label are warned/skipped by intake — sources.py:_derive_type_from_labels requires exactly one of RECOGNIZED_STORY_TYPES, and sprint/shape_gate.py skips issues that fail entry shape — so slices could be created but never schedulable, which is the failure mode AC 4's 'runnable' framing exists to prevent.
  Suggestion: State in Step 1 that each gh issue create carries the original's type label and milestone (runbook §'Label and milestone at creation'), and add a Step 5 assertion that the rendered create args include a recognized type label.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 3 (retry after partial creation duplicates slice issues). The mitigation — stable decomposition markers plus a persisted slice-id→issue-number map — is stated but no step verifies it: Step 5 covers 'actionable reporting of already-created slices', not idempotent re-entry. The gate's resume path (preflight_complexity_gate.py:430-441) honours a recorded prior decision, so a run interrupted mid-apply and resumed re-enters with decision='accept' already on state.
  Suggestion: Add a Step 5 case that re-runs apply against a state carrying a partial slice map and asserts no duplicate creates, and make Step 2 explicit about what the resume path does when application status is 'partial'.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 puts the whole apply path in a new coordinator module without saying how it reaches gh. The repo already has issue-creation call sites (cli/todo.py, cli/author.py, cli/baseline_fix.py) and issue-fetch helpers in sprint/shape_gate.py:_fetch_issue_detail; a fourth ad-hoc subprocess shape is avoidable.
  Suggestion: Reuse the existing gh invocation helper rather than adding a new subprocess wrapper, or note in Step 1 which one is being reused.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Plan risk 3 (retry after partial creation could duplicate slice issues) is carried, not retired: Steps 1 and 3 persist the slice-id-to-issue-number map and report created issues, but no step implements or tests consulting that map (or the proposed body markers) to skip already-created slices on a re-run. This does not threaten an acceptance criterion — the ACs require an actionable partial-failure state, which the plan delivers — but the dedup-on-retry behavior named in the mitigation is left to the dev agent.
  Suggestion: In decomposition_application.py, before creating each slice, check the persisted created-slice records (and optionally search for the stable decomposition marker) and reuse the existing issue number instead of creating a duplicate; add a test case for resuming after a mid-apply failure.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 2's constraint pair — add accept/decline to the operator vocabulary while keeping normalize_preflight_gate_no_decision restricted to non-accepting actions — cannot be met by simply extending the PREFLIGHT_GATE_ACTIONS tuple, because that tuple is used both to build pending-record options (preflight_complexity_gate.py:589) and to validate the no-decision fallback (config/types.py:812) and prior/normalized decisions (preflight_complexity_gate.py:431,630,641). The dev agent must split it into two vocabularies (all gate options vs. fallback-eligible actions) and audit each existing membership check for which set it needs.
  Suggestion: Introduce a separate tuple (e.g. PREFLIGHT_GATE_PROPOSAL_ACTIONS or a combined PREFLIGHT_GATE_ALL_ACTIONS) and update each of the five call sites deliberately; Step 6's test that timeout can never resolve to accept will catch mistakes.
